primary_diagnosis_treated: Essential hypertension (stage 1) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia and prediabetes

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily; increase to 5 mg after 2 weeks if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually (BP, renal function, potassium)
medications.purpose: First‑line treatment of stage 1 hypertension (patient <55 yr, non‑Afro‑Caribbean) per NICE NG136
medications.nice_justification: NG136 – Step 1 monotherapy for hypertension in adults <55 yr not of Afro‑Caribbean origin

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce LDL‑C in heterozygous FH; achieve ≥40 % reduction per CG126
medications.nice_justification: CG126 – High‑intensity statin is first‑line for heterozygous FH

medications.dose: 500 mg orally twice daily (start 500 mg once daily, increase after 1 week if tolerated)
medications.duration: If eGFR ≥45 ml/min/1.73 m² – continue until HbA1c <6.0 % or weight loss achieved; review HbA1c at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Improve glycaemic control in prediabetes with additional cardiovascular risk (NICE NG28)
medications.nice_justification: NG28 – Metformin may be offered to adults with prediabetes when lifestyle alone is unlikely to achieve control and renal function permits

interactions_checked.action: No dose adjustment needed; monitor renal function and potassium as per ACE‑I monitoring

treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 5 mg) as first‑line antihypertensive, initiate high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg nightly for heterozygous FH, and consider metformin 500 mg BID for prediabetes after confirming eGFR ≥45 ml/min/1.73 m². Provide lifestyle advice (salt <6 g/day, DASH diet, regular exercise, weight management, smoking cessation). Monitor BP, renal function, electrolytes, LFTs, lipid profile, and HbA1c according to NICE NG136, CG126, and NG28. Avoid chronic NSAIDs and dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy.
